title: Strings: Slicing, Methods, and Formatting
description: Master string manipulation in Python, from advanced slicing to core methods and f-strings.

blocks.content: A title typed by an editor has extra spaces and mixed capitals. You need to reshape text before it becomes a URL. What could you ask Python to do here?

## Advanced Slicing: `[start:stop:step]`

You can extract sub-strings with slice notation:

```python
text = "PythonProgramming"
print(text[0:6])     # 'Python' (from index 0 up to, but not including, 6)
print(text[6:])      # 'Programming' (from index 6 to end)
print(text[::2])     # 'PtoPormig' (every second character)
print(text[::-1])    # 'gnimmargorPnohtyP' (reversed!)
```

```mermaid
graph LR
    P["0: P"] --- Y["1: y"] --- T["2: t"] --- H["3: h"] --- O["4: o"] --- N["5: n"]
```

Text has positions, like letters in a word or seats in a row. Indexing and slicing let you look at one character or a stretch of characters.

Python counts from zero, so the first character is position 0. A slice stops before its end position, which is a common off-by-one surprise.

blocks.question: What does `'statica'[1:5]` evaluate to?
blocks.explanation: Indices 1 through 4 (stopping before 5) are: index 1 ('t'), 2 ('a'), 3 ('t'), 4 ('i'), producing 'tati'.

blocks.starterCode:
raw_url = "https://example.com/api/v1/users/profile"

# Check protocol
is_secure = raw_url.startswith("https://")
print(f"Is HTTPS: {is_secure}")

# Extract path segments
segments = raw_url.replace("https://", "").split("/")
print(f"Domain: {segments[0]}")
print(f"Path: {' / '.join(segments[1:])}")

Write a function `clean_and_slugify(title)` that cleans a blog post title by converting it to lowercase, stripping surrounding whitespace, and replacing spaces with hyphens `-`.

Example:
`clean_and_slugify("  Learn Python Fast  ")` -> `"learn-python-fast"`
